BILL NUMBER:  S2394

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the general municipal law, in relation to establishing
criteria for notice of claim to be filed and served when done by
electronic means in a city having a population of over one million


 PURPOSE :
To require any city with a population of over one million inhabitants
to accept service of a notice of claim filed by electronic means.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :
Section one amends section 50-e of the General Municipal Law by adding
a new paragraph (e) to subdivision 3 to allow a notice of claim to be
filed electronically through the Internet in any city with a
population of over one million. The new section would also provide
that any notice of claim that is filed by electronic means shall
contain the same information as required for a written notice and a
declaration certifying the truth of the contents of the notice.

Section two amends subdivision 5 of section 50-e of the General
Municipal Law by authorizing the courts, when considering whether to
grant a motion to a claimant who applies to the court to file a late
notice of claim, to consider whether claimant's failure to file a
timely notice of claim was due to the technical failure of the
computer system of the public corporation, the claimant or the
claimant's attorney. The claimant or attorney must provide sufficient
proof that the electronic service was attempted in a timely manner.

Section three sets forth the effective date of the bill.

 JUSTIFICATION :
Filing a Notice of Claim is a prerequisite to the commencement of a
tort-based action against a public corporation.  When claims are
against a public corporation, such as New York City, the provisions of
section 50-e of the General Municipal Law control.  Currently, section
50-e (3) of the General Municipal Law requires service of the Notice
of Claim to be made personally, or by registered or certified mail.

In light of new technology and the public's increasing reliance on the
Internet, claimants or their attorneys may benefit from the ease of
electronically filing their Notice of Claim. Not only will filing the
Notice of Claim electronically result in a faster and less costly
means of transmission, but also, and perhaps more importantly, a means
that is less prone to human error. Moreover, both the public
corporation and the public will benefit because the public corporation
will be able to store and manage records in a more efficient manner.

New York has realized the practical and beneficial effects of using
technology in the service process of various types of claims. For
example, in 1989, an amendment was made to CPLR 2103 (b)(5) to allow
attorneys to serve court papers via facsimile. Further, in 1999, an
amendment was made to CPLR 2103(b)(7) to allow service via electronic
means, which now allows service of court papers by attorneys over the
Internet. More recently, in 2003, the New York State Court of Claims
began the Filing by Electronic Means pilot project, which allows
certain claims to be filed and served via e-mail. To date, the pilot
project is still running.

In 2006, a similar bill was vetoed on the grounds that the bill could
inadvertently increase the number of motions to file a late notice
since there was no means to ascertain whether a filing, delay was, in
fact, due to a computer system failure. The current bill addresses
this concern.

Moreover, due to concerns that many public corporations throughout the
State, especially those who retain private attorneys to represent the
public corporation, may not be prepared to adopt this new process,
this bill will be limited to notices of claim served upon any city
with a population of over one million inhabitants.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
2007; A.8996-A/S.6122- Passed Assembly/S. Rules Committee 2006 -
A.11919; Veto Memo
317

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
On the one hundred and eightieth day after it shall have become law.

summary: Establishes criteria for notice to be filed and served when done by electronic means in a city having a population of more than one million; provides for an application for leave to serve a late notice.
